summary: Fire lookout in Itasca County, MN, marked gone; a Forest Lookouts entry for Winnie Dam records 1972 bids to sell the tower.

facts.status_note: Fire Lookout Association lists it as gone; the sources read give no removal date

events.note: Bids opened for the sale of the tower on June 8, 1972, per the Forest Lookouts entry for Winnie Dam

evidence.supports: Winnie is in Itasca County and marked gone on the association's county list
the Forest Lookouts Minnesota page has an entry titled Winnie Dam
the Winnie Dam entry places the tower in Itasca County and the Chippewa National Forest, at township 146N, range 26W, section 30
bids were opened for the sale of the tower on June 8, 1972; the entry says airplane patrols had proven superior to the towers
evidence.quote: June 8, 1972: Bids were opened for the sale of the tower, airplane patrols have proven to be superior to the towers.

evidence.supports: a Forest Service handbook lists a Winnie Dam camp and picnic ground on the eastern tip of Lake Winnibigoshish
evidence.quote: Winnie Dam Camp and Picnic Grounds on the eastern tip of Winnibigoshish.

sources.title: Chippewa National Forest
sources.publisher: U.S. Forest Service handbook, hosted by npshistory.com

notes_for_editor: Identity is inferred. The association's 'Winnie' record (Itasca, 47.43888, -94.03352) and the Forest Lookouts 'Winnie Dam' entry (Itasca County, T146N R26W S30) share a name and county, but no source we read ties them together, and the coordinates were not checked against the township and section. The only dated item in the sources read is the 1972 sale bids; the entry does not say the tower was sold or removed. No build date, height or staffing was found. The Forest Service handbook page is about a camp, not the tower, and its date was not visible in our fetch. Do not use Wikipedia's Winnie Cumulus Broadcasting Tower (Winnie, Texas): it is a different structure. A Star Tribune article on removed Minnesota towers was rate-limited (HTTP 429) and not read. Suggested check: Chippewa National Forest or Minnesota DNR records for the 1972 sale and the removal.
